upgrades.label: Smart guest-room thermostats and occupancy sensing
upgrades.description: Sets vacant and away rooms back and recovers when a guest returns.

comfort.note: Rooms need recovery time when a guest returns; check the recovery setting.

upgrades.source: Setback: 5 F mid, the minimum unoccupied setback required by the Illinois Statewide Technical Reference Manual (IL-TRM v5.0, Guest Room Energy Management) and used in the California 2013 CASE report; 3 F and 7 F are PLACEHOLDER bounds. Cost: $260 per room incremental cost (IL-TRM v5.0); range $100 to $500 per room (California 2013 CASE, Guest Room Occupancy Controls). Life: 15 years (IL-TRM). Cross-check: a DOE/PNNL field study (2012) measured 10.8% to 26.5% (average 18.4%) of guest-room HVAC energy saved. Values seen in search excerpts of these documents; to confirm in the primary texts.

upgrades.label: Roof and envelope insulation
upgrades.description: Cuts the weather-driven heating and cooling load.
upgrades.source: Weather-load reduction mid 10%: consistent with NREL ComStock roof insulation to ASHRAE AEDG levels (about 11% of gas heating and 12% of electric heating, stock-wide). Low and high: PLACEHOLDER. Cost: PLACEHOLDER $3.50 per ft2 of roof (contractor ranges $2 to $7 per ft2 for insulation only). Life: PLACEHOLDER.

upgrades.label: LED lighting retrofit
upgrades.description: Replaces remaining non-LED lamps and fixtures throughout the hotel.
upgrades.source: Lighting reduction: low 27% (linear LED replacing fluorescent, PNNL evaluation for GSA), high 60% (incandescent-heavy fixtures); mid 45% is a judgment between them for a mixed hotel stock. Life: 12 years (IL-TRM default for LED fixtures when rated hours are unknown). Cost: PLACEHOLDER $0.40/$0.60/$0.90 per ft2 (no credible source found yet). Values seen in search excerpts; to confirm.

upgrades.label: Occupancy sensors in common areas and hallways
upgrades.description: Dims or turns off lighting and trims ventilation in unoccupied public areas.

comfort.note: A missed detection can leave a space dark; set sensible time delays.

upgrades.source: Lighting reduction in common areas and hallways: mid 24%, the average occupancy-sensor saving in the LBNL meta-analysis (Williams et al., LBNL-5095E, 2011); high 45% from PNNL stairwell assumptions (10% occupancy, 50% light reduction when vacant); low 12% is a PLACEHOLDER. Ventilation reduction, cost and life: PLACEHOLDER. Values seen in search excerpts; to confirm.

upgrades.label: Energy management controls (scheduling and optimization)
upgrades.description: Schedules and tunes the central plant, public-area HVAC and fans.

comfort.note: Poorly set schedules can reduce comfort; commissioning matters.

upgrades.source: HVAC reduction 4/7/10%: consistent with a 3% whole-building median saving for lodging retro-commissioning (Crowe, Mills et al. 2020, Energy and Buildings, about 1,500 buildings), which is about 7.6% of HVAC energy if all of it is HVAC (39.5% HVAC share, CBECS 2018 lodging). Cost: PLACEHOLDER $15,000 + $0.20 per ft2; for comparison the retro-commissioning median is $0.26 per ft2 (Crowe 2020), without control hardware. Life: PLACEHOLDER. Values seen in search excerpts; to confirm.

upgrades.label: High-efficiency HVAC equipment
upgrades.description: Replaces the heating and cooling equipment with higher-efficiency units, sized from the reduced load.
upgrades.source: Heating reduction mid 13%: replacing an 80% efficient boiler (typical existing stock, GSA evaluation) with a condensing boiler at about 92% seasonal efficiency gives 1 - 0.80/0.92 = 13%; NREL ComStock (Condensing Gas Boilers, 2025) reports 9% site savings for an example building. Low and high, cooling reduction, cost and life: PLACEHOLDER. Values seen in search excerpts; to confirm.

upgrades.label: High-efficiency water heating and low-flow fixtures
upgrades.description: Condensing water heaters and low-flow fixtures.

comfort.note: Guests may notice lower flow at fixtures.

upgrades.source: PLACEHOLDER. Replace with ENERGY STAR and DOE hotel water-heating guidance.

upgrades.label: Rooftop solar
upgrades.description: Sized to the usable roof (never above the hotel's yearly electricity use). Output comes from the location's solar data; the hotel uses what it can hour by hour and any surplus is exported at the region's export credit. Yearly operation and maintenance is subtracted.
upgrades.source: Sizing: PLACEHOLDER usable roof share (0.5) and roof area per kW (100 ft2). Output: the climate's solar data. Cost: the region's installed cost per W. Operation and maintenance: $17.63 per kW (DC) a year for commercial PV in 2024 ($14.17 system plus $3.46 administration), NREL/NLR Annual Technology Baseline 2025, Commercial PV (seen in a search excerpt; to confirm in the ATB table). Degradation: 0.5% a year, consistent with Jordan et al. 2022, Progress in Photovoltaics (NREL/TP-5K00-81314): fleet median 0.75% a year, cooler climates 0.48% a year. Inverter replacement is not included.

source: Upgrade values are a mix of researched figures (named in each upgrade's source, from search excerpts still to confirm in the primary documents) and placeholders, labelled as such.
